name: Śāṇḍilya's meditation (Śāṇḍilya-vidyā)
method_summary: In tranquillity, venerate all this as brahman — that from which it arises, into which it dissolves and by which it breathes; form one's resolve, since one becomes on departing what one resolves here; meditate on the self in the heart, made of mind, with breath as body and light as form, smaller than a grain and greater than the worlds, as brahman to be attained on departing, without doubt.
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: Meditation on the small space in the heart (dahara-vidyā)
method_summary: Seek and understand what is within the small space in the lotus of the heart, in this 'city of brahman': as large as outer space, containing heaven and earth; the self free from evil, old age, death, sorrow, hunger and thirst, whose desires and intentions are real.
signs_of_progress: freedom of movement in all worlds; whatever one desires arises by intention (ChU 8.1.6-8.2)
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: The honey-doctrine (madhu-vidyā)
method_summary: ChU 3.1-11: meditate on the sun as the honey of the gods, the Vedas as flowers and the rays as honeycomb cells; for one who knows it the sun neither rises nor sets. BAU 2.5 (also called the madhu-brāhmaṇa): meditate on earth, waters, fire and all things as 'honey' for all beings and all beings as honey for them, culminating in 'this self is brahman'.

warnings.text: To be taught only to one's eldest son or a worthy pupil (ChU 3.11.5-6).

notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: Meditation on the self common to all men (vaiśvānara-vidyā)
method_summary: Venerate the vaiśvānara self as the whole — sky as head, sun as eye, wind as breath, space as trunk, water as bladder, earth as feet — 'a span in size and beyond measure', not as any one of its parts; the first morsels of food are then offered into it as an agnihotra.

warnings.text: Each partial meditation is incomplete, and the king says each would have come to harm (losing head, sight, breath...) without the whole teaching (ChU 5.12-17).

notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: Meditation on the five fires (pañcāgni-vidyā)
method_summary: Know yonder world, the rain-god, this world, man and woman as five sacrificial fires into which faith, Soma, rain, food and semen are offered; knowing this (with faith and austerity) one goes by the path of the gods and is not stained even by association with those who fall.
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: The meditation on plenitude (bhūma-vidyā)
method_summary: Venerate in ascending order name, speech, mind, intention, thought, meditation, understanding, strength, food, water, heat, space, memory, hope and breath as brahman, each greater than the one before; then seek to understand truth, understanding, thinking, faith, steadfastness, action and happiness, up to plenitude (bhūman), where one sees nothing else; then the teaching of 'I' and of the self.
signs_of_progress: freedom of movement as far as each object reaches; the self-ruled moves at will in all worlds (ChU 7.25.2)
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: The teaching of being (sad-vidyā)
method_summary: Uddālaka's method: by one lump of clay all clay is known; in the beginning was being alone; it made heat, water and food threefold; illustrated by sleep, dying, honey, rivers, the tree, the banyan seed, salt, the blindfolded man and the axe ordeal, each ending 'that you are'.
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: Upakosala's meditation (upakosala-vidyā)
method_summary: Venerate breath, joy (ka) and space (kha) as brahman, the fires as its forms, and the person seen in the eye as the self, the immortal, the fearless, brahman; the knower goes by the path of light and does not return.
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: The meditation on the gatherer (saṃvarga-vidyā)
method_summary: Venerate wind as the gatherer into which fire, sun, moon and waters go (with respect to the gods) and breath as the gatherer into which speech, sight, hearing and mind go in sleep (with respect to the self).
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: Satyakāma's meditation on the four quarters of brahman
method_summary: Venerate brahman as having four quarters of four parts each — the quarters of space ('shining'), earth, mid-space, sky and ocean ('endless'), fire, sun, moon and lightning ('luminous'), breath, sight, hearing and mind ('having an abode') — as taught to Satyakāma by a bull, fire, a goose and a diver-bird.
notes: Names of the quarters from memory (moderate). Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: The meditation on the person as sacrifice (puruṣa-vidyā)
method_summary: Regard one's life as a soma sacrifice: the first twenty-four years as the morning pressing, the next forty-four as the midday, the next forty-eight as the evening; hunger and thirst as consecration; austerity, giving, uprightness, non-injury and truthfulness as the priestly gifts; death as the final bath.
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: Meditation on the Gāyatrī
method_summary: Venerate the Gāyatrī as all this — speech, earth, body, heart — whose four feet are the worlds, the Vedas, the breaths and the sun; and the space within the heart as identical with the space outside (ChU 3.12; BAU 5.14).

name: Meditation on the imperishable (akṣara-vidyā)
method_summary: Know the imperishable by the negations 'not gross, not fine, not short, not long...' and as that by whose command sun and moon stand apart; without this knowledge all rites are finite.
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: Pratardana's meditation on breath as the intelligent self
method_summary: Venerate Indra/breath as the intelligent self (prajñātman), as life and immortality; know not speech but the speaker, not the object but the knower.
notes: Brahma Sūtra 1.1.28-31 discusses this passage. Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: The meditation taught to Bālāki
method_summary: Pass beyond venerating the persons in the sun, moon and other phenomena as brahman to the self into which the sleeper withdraws and from which all breaths, worlds and gods come forth.
notes: Upaniṣadic 'vidyā' (meditation-knowledge); the Brahma Sūtra (3.3) discusses which vidyās are to be combined.

name: Meditation on the person in the eye
method_summary: Venerate the person seen in the eye as the self, the immortal, the fearless, brahman.

warnings.text: Virocana misunderstood 'the person seen in the eye' as the body and its reflection (ChU 8.7-8).

name: Meditation on the vyāhṛtis
method_summary: Meditate on bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, suvaḥ and mahaḥ as the worlds, lights, Vedas and breaths, mahaḥ being brahman, the self (TU 1.5-6).

name: Meditation on combinations (saṃhitā)
method_summary: Meditate on the five great combinations — of worlds, lights, knowledge, progeny and the body — each as prior form, latter form, junction and link (TU 1.3).

name: Meditation on the udgītha
method_summary: Venerate the syllable Om as the udgītha, the highest essence, and the udgītha as the breath in the mouth untouched by evil; what is done with knowledge, faith and the upaniṣad is more powerful (ChU 1.1-1.12; BAU 1.3).

name: Meditation on Om (praṇava-upāsanā)
method_summary: Meditate on the self as Om; Om is the bow, the self the arrow, brahman the target, to be pierced by one who is undistracted (MuU 2.2.3-6); the body as lower fire-stick and Om as upper, by the friction of meditation one sees God (ŚU 1.14); meditating on Om with one, two or three measures until death leads to the human world, the moon or the brahma-world (PrU 5); A, U, M and the measureless correspond to the four quarters (MāU); Om as the best support (KU 1.2.15-17).

equivalents.note: Yoga Sūtra 1.27-28 repetition of Om (U10); the Upaniṣads speak of meditation (upāsanā, abhidhyāna) rather than repetition

name: Meditation on breath as brahman
method_summary: Venerate breath as the eldest and best, as brahman (KauU 2.1-2; ChU 4.10.4), as life and immortality (KauU 3.2); know its food and clothing (BAU 6.1.14; ChU 5.2).

name: Venerating it as the self
method_summary: 'One should venerate it as the self alone, for in it all these become one' — not as any single function (breathing, speaking, seeing), each of which is incomplete; venerate the self alone as dear (BAU 1.4.7-8).

name: The inner fire-offering of Pratardana
method_summary: Recognizing that while one speaks one cannot breathe and while one breathes one cannot speak, one regards speaking as offering breath into speech and breathing as offering speech into breath — two endless offerings made continually, waking or asleep, in place of the outer agnihotra.

equivalents.note: both internalize the agnihotra into the breaths; the ChU form offers food into the five breaths

name: Offering food into the breaths (prāṇāgnihotra)
method_summary: The first morsels of each meal are offered with 'to prāṇa svāhā', then to vyāna, apāna, samāna and udāna; each offering satisfies the corresponding sense, deity and world; done with knowledge it is an agnihotra into the vaiśvānara self that burns up all evils.

name: Hearing (śravaṇa)
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): 'the self should be seen, heard, reflected upon and meditated upon'; hearing is the second of the four verbs (BAU 2.4.5, 4.5.6).

name: Reflection (manana)
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): 'the self should be ... reflected upon (mantavya)' (BAU 2.4.5, 4.5.6).

name: Deep contemplation (nididhyāsana)
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): 'the self should be ... meditated upon (nididhyāsitavya)'; by seeing, hearing, reflecting on and understanding the self all this is known (BAU 2.4.5, 4.5.6).

name: Negation: 'not so, not so'
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): the self or brahman is indicated by the instruction 'not so, not so', denying of it every graspable form — it is ungraspable, indestructible, unattached, unbound (BAU 2.3.6, 3.9.26, 4.2.4, 4.4.22, 4.5.15); the text states it as an instruction (ādeśa), not as a graded exercise.

name: Yoga of the inner self (Kaṭha)
method_summary: Realize the hidden god in the cave by the yoga of the inner self (KU 1.2.12); turn the gaze inward (2.1.1); restrain speech into mind, mind into the self that is knowledge, that into the great self, that into the peaceful self (1.3.13); yoga is the firm holding of the senses, when the five senses and mind stand still and the intellect does not stir (2.3.10-11); draw the thumb-sized person out of the body like the stalk from muñja grass (2.3.17).
signs_of_progress: the highest state: senses and mind still, intellect not stirring (KU 2.3.10)

warnings.text: 'Then one becomes undistracted, for yoga is arising and passing away' — the text warns that the state is unstable without vigilance (KU 2.3.11, one reading).
One who has not ceased from bad conduct, is not calm or collected cannot attain it (KU 1.2.24).

name: The yoga of the Śvetāśvatara (posture, breath, place)
method_summary: Hold the body steady with chest, neck and head erect; draw the senses with the mind into the heart; restrain the breaths, with movements controlled, and breathe out gently through the nose when the breath is diminished; hold the mind attentively like a chariot yoked to unruly horses; practise in a level, clean place free of pebbles, fire, sand, noise and damp, pleasing to the mind and sheltered from wind.
prerequisites: the invocations of Savitṛ to yoke the mind (ŚU 2.1-7)
signs_of_progress: forms like fog, smoke, sun, wind, fire, fireflies, lightning, crystal and moon precede brahman's manifestation; lightness, health, freedom from craving, clear complexion, pleasant voice and smell, scant excreta (ŚU 2.11-13)

warnings.text: The place must be free of disturbances (pebbles, fire, sand, noise, water-places) and not offend the eye (ŚU 2.10).
The breath is to be let out gently through the nose when diminished (ŚU 2.9).

name: The six-limbed yoga of the Maitrī
method_summary: Breath-control, withdrawal of the senses, meditation, concentration, contemplative reasoning (tarka) and absorption; the text adds placing the mind in the no-mind and the breath in the fourth (6.19), a concentration by restraining speech, mind and breath with a gesture of the tongue at the palate, seeing brahman by tarka (6.20), and rising through the suṣumṇā joined with breath, Om and mind (6.21).
signs_of_progress: seeing the golden-coloured maker; faults do not approach the knower, as animals avoid a burning mountain (6.18); becoming selfless (nirātman), the mark of liberation (6.20)

equivalents.note: shares prāṇāyāma, pratyāhāra, dhyāna, dhāraṇā and samādhi with Patañjali's limbs but has tarka and a different order

notes: Recorded as the text states it; later haṭha elaborations of the palate practice (khecarī) are restricted and belong to other units. Distinct from the Kālacakra six-branch yoga.

name: Breath-control (prāṇāyāma)
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): first limb of the Maitrī's yoga (6.18); ŚU 2.9: restraining the breaths with movements controlled, breathe out through the nose when the breath is diminished.

warnings.text: Breath is let out gently, through the nose (ŚU 2.9).

name: Withdrawal of the senses (pratyāhāra)
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): second limb in MaiU 6.18; draw the senses with the mind into the heart (ŚU 2.8); turn the sight inward (KU 2.1.1); draw all the senses into the self (ChU 8.15.1).

name: Concentration (dhāraṇā)
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): yoga as 'the firm holding (dhāraṇā) of the senses' (KU 2.3.11); fourth limb in MaiU 6.18; 'its further concentration' at the palate (MaiU 6.20).

name: Meditation (dhyāna)
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): venerate meditation as brahman (ChU 7.6); by the yoga of meditation the sages saw God's power (ŚU 1.3); the friction of meditation with Om (ŚU 1.14); 'meditating, one sees him' (MuU 3.1.8); a limb in MaiU 6.18.

name: Absorption (samādhi)
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): the sixth limb of the Maitrī's yoga (6.18); 'the happiness of a mind whose stains are washed away by samādhi cannot be described' (MaiU 6.34); being 'collected' (samāhita) in BAU 4.4.23 and KU 1.2.24.

name: Listening to the inner sound
method_summary: The Upaniṣads mention hearing an inner sound with the ears closed: the roar or crackling of fire heard when one closes the ears is the light within (ChU 3.13.8); the sound of the digestive fire, no longer heard when one is about to depart (BAU 5.9.1); closing the ears with the thumbs one hears the sound of the space within the heart in seven forms and passes beyond it into the soundless brahman (MaiU 6.22).
signs_of_progress: the seven sounds of MaiU 6.22: like rivers, a small bell, a bronze vessel, a wheel, frogs, rain, a voice in a sheltered place
notes: Later haṭha and yoga Upaniṣads elaborate nāda practice (U28/U29).

name: The three 'da': self-restraint, giving, compassion
method_summary: Practise the three that the thunder repeats — da, da, da: be restrained (dāmyata), give (datta), be compassionate (dayadhvam) (BAU 5.2).

name: The food vows (Taittirīya)
method_summary: Do not despise food; do not reject food; make much food; turn no one away from your dwelling — each is called a vow (vrata) (TU 3.7-10).

name: Purity of food (āhāraśuddhi)
method_summary: When food (what is taken in) is pure, the mind is pure; when the mind is pure, memory is firm; with firm memory all knots are loosened (ChU 7.26.2).
signs_of_progress: firm memory (dhruvā smṛti); loosening of all knots

name: Austerity (tapas)
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): Bhṛgu seeks brahman by tapas (TU 3.1-6); a year of austerity, celibacy and faith before questioning (PrU 1.2); the self is found by truth and austerity (MuU 3.1.5; ŚU 1.15); austerity as a branch of dharma (ChU 2.23.1).

warnings.text: Rites and austerities performed without knowing the imperishable come to an end (BAU 3.8.10).

name: Studentship and celibacy (brahmacarya)
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): what people call sacrifice, offering, the long session, silence, fasting and forest-life is really brahmacarya (ChU 8.5); the brahma-world belongs to those who find it by brahmacarya (8.4.3); living in the teacher's house (ChU 2.23.1; 8.15.1).

name: Recitation and teaching of the Veda (svādhyāya-pravacana)
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): every duty is to be joined with study and teaching of the Veda; 'study and teaching alone, for that is austerity' (TU 1.9); 'do not neglect your study' (TU 1.11).

name: Giving (dāna)
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): 'give' (datta, BAU 5.2); give with faith, grace, modesty, awe and understanding (TU 1.11.3); giving among the priestly gifts of the life-sacrifice (ChU 3.17.4).

name: Non-injury (ahiṃsā)
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): non-injury among the priestly gifts of the life-sacrifice (ChU 3.17.4); not harming any creature except at sacred places (ChU 8.15.1).

name: Truthfulness (satya)
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): 'speak the truth' (TU 1.11.1); truth alone conquers (MuU 3.1.6); truthful speech among the priestly gifts (ChU 3.17.4); the truthful is not burned (ChU 6.16).

name: Approaching a teacher with fuel in hand
method_summary: Having become disgusted with the worlds won by action, go 'fuel in hand' to a teacher learned in the Veda and established in brahman (MuU 1.2.12); live with the teacher a set time in austerity, celibacy and faith before asking (PrU 1.2); serve the teacher (ChU 4.4-9, 8.7-12, 8.15).

name: Devotion to the teacher (guru-bhakti)
method_summary: Hold the highest devotion to God and to one's teacher as to God (ŚU 6.23); honour the teacher as a god (TU 1.11.2); the pupils worship Pippalāda as the father who takes them across (PrU 6.8).

name: Going for refuge (śaraṇāgati)
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): 'I, desiring liberation, go for refuge to that God who illumines the understanding of the self' (ŚU 6.18).

name: Renunciation (saṃnyāsa)
method_summary: Rising above the desires for sons, wealth and worlds, living as a mendicant on alms, wandering forth for the sake of the self (BAU 3.5.1, 4.4.22); ascetics purified by the yoga of renunciation (MuU 3.2.6); forest-dwelling with austerity and faith on alms (MuU 1.2.11); after the father-son transfer the recovered father may wander as a mendicant (KauU 2.15).
notes: The rules of the renunciant orders are in the Saṃnyāsa Upaniṣads (U04) and later texts (U57).

name: The head-vow (śirovrata)
method_summary: A vow whose performance, 'according to rule', qualifies one to be taught the knowledge of brahman (MuU 3.2.10-11); the text does not describe it.
notes: Commentators differ on its nature; not reconstructed here.

name: The father-to-son transfer at death (sampratti)
method_summary: A dying father transfers his roles and faculties to his son: 'you are brahman, the sacrifice, the world' (BAU 1.5.17); or lying on the son and placing speech, breath, sight and the other faculties in him one by one, the son receiving each (KauU 2.15).

name: The prayer of the dying (Īśa 15-18)
method_summary: At death one asks Pūṣan to uncover the face of truth covered by the golden vessel, affirms 'that person yonder, I am he', commits breath to the wind and body to ashes, bids the mind remember what was done, and asks Agni to lead by the good path (Īśa 15-18; BAU 5.15).

name: Remembering at the time of death
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): 'O mind, remember what was done' (Īśa 17); at death take refuge in the imperishable, the unshaken, the essence of breath (ChU 3.17.6); meditating on Om until death (PrU 5.1); as one's resolve, so one becomes (ChU 3.14.1).

name: Departure through the crown at death
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): at death one goes up through the channel to the crown and reaches immortality (KU 2.3.16; ChU 8.6.6); saying 'Om' one rises by the sun's rays (ChU 8.6.5); the person made of mind goes out through the indrayoni (TU 1.6); through the suṣumṇā joined with breath, Om and mind one goes upward (MaiU 6.21). Summary only.

name: The mantha rite
method_summary: A rite for one who desires greatness, performed after an observance, in which offerings of ghee are made to the breaths and other deities and a prepared mixture is drunk with formulas (BAU 6.3; ChU 5.2.4-8). Summary only.

warnings.text: It should not be taught to anyone but a son or a pupil (BAU 6.3.12).

name: Procreation rites (BAU 6.4)
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Upaniṣadic): BAU 6.4 treats marital union as a sacrificial act with rites for conception and offspring. Recorded as a summary only (sexual rite).
notes: Summary only under the restricted-content rule; no procedures, formulas or details reproduced.
